title: Your $1,200 Phone Costs 48 Hours Of Work

beats.say: A twelve hundred dollar phone is not twelve hundred dollars. It is forty eight hours of your life.
beats.visual: a sleek dark smartphone lying on a stack of time cards under a cold desk lamp, extreme close-up, no text, no people

beats.say: There is a simple rule. Before any purchase, divide the price by what you earn in an hour after tax.
beats.visual: a hand holding a pocket calculator over a wooden desk in warm morning light, no faces

beats.say: Say you take home twenty five dollars an hour. That is your exchange rate between money and time.
beats.visual: an old brass clock face with a gold coin balanced on the hour hand, dramatic dark background

beats.say: Twelve hundred divided by twenty five is forty eight. Six full workdays for one phone.
beats.visual: a wall calendar with six consecutive days crossed out in red marker, close-up, soft light

beats.say: Does that change how it feels? For some, yes. For others, the phone is still worth it. Both are fine.
beats.visual: a fork in a quiet forest path under soft backlight, two directions, no people

beats.say: Now try something small. A five dollar coffee every workday is about twelve hundred fifty dollars a year.
beats.visual: a steaming paper cup of coffee on a worn desk beside a stack of coins, morning window light

beats.say: Here is the part nobody tells you. That is fifty hours of work a year. More than a full workweek, on one habit.
beats.visual: a stopwatch ticking on a dark table with a long time trail behind it, long exposure

beats.say: Now flip it. A three thousand dollar vacation is one hundred twenty hours. Fifteen workdays for a trip you will remember.
beats.visual: a lone tropical beach at sunrise with golden light on calm water, wide shot, no people

beats.say: This rule does not tell you to stop spending. It tells you what you are actually trading.
beats.visual: a pair of balanced brass scales with a gold coin on one side and an hourglass on the other

beats.say: So here is the move. Find your hourly number tonight. Write it on a card in your wallet.
beats.visual: a small white index card with a pen beside it on a dark wooden table, close-up, no text visible

beats.say: Next time you hover over the buy button, divide first. Then decide.
beats.visual: a finger hovering over a glowing phone screen in a dark room, extreme close-up, no faces

beats.say: Spend on what is worth your hours. Skip what is not. Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: an empty highway stretching toward a glowing sunrise horizon, wide shot

caption: Price divided by your after-tax hourly pay. A $1,200 phone at $25 an hour is 48 hours of work. Spend on what is worth your hours. Educational content, not financial advice.
description: A simple rule: divide any price by your after-tax hourly pay to see what you trade for it. A $1,200 phone at $25 an hour is 48 hours, six workdays.
first_comment: What is the last thing you bought that was clearly worth the hours? Educational only, not financial advice.

facts.claim: $5 a workday x 250 workdays = $1,250 a year = 50 hours at $25
